dedupe_keys.name: singapore cyber landscape annual csa statistics on ransomware phishing defacements and infected systems 2016 to 2025 2026

description: The Singapore Cyber Landscape is the annual review by the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore, which also runs the national CERT, SingCERT. Ten editions are listed, from 2016 to 2025/2026. Each reviews malicious cyber activity seen in Singapore over the past year, gives yearly counts with a short trend, and describes national measures for critical information infrastructure. The 2025/2026 edition (58 pages) reports 165 ransomware cases reported to CSA in 2025 against 132, 132 and 159 in 2022 to 2024, with wholesale and retail, manufacturing and construction the most affected industries. It reports 62 defaced Singapore websites against 340, 108 and 67 in the three previous years, and describes phishing trends and a sharp rise in infected infrastructure driven by vulnerable consumer IoT devices and malware-as-a-service. Chapters contributed by Cloudflare, Google Threat Intelligence and the Singapore Police Force cover DDoS, supply-chain compromises and scams. Coverage: Singapore, annual, 2016 to 2025. Format and access: PDF and flipbook, free download. Caveats: figures count cases reported to or observed by CSA, so under-reporting is likely, as the report says for phishing; categories and methods change between editions; there are no machine-readable tables. Simulation uses: annual base rates of ransomware and defacement incidents for cyber threat scenarios against a small, highly digitalised economy. Related records: the HKCERT security incident statistics, the JPCERT/CC quarterly incident reports and the Traficom Autoreporter statistics give comparable national incident series.
name: Singapore Cyber Landscape: annual CSA statistics on ransomware, phishing, defacements and infected systems (2016 to 2025/2026)
notes: Publications list and the 2025/2026 page read with curl on 2026-09-26; the 2025/2026 PDF was read for its figures and deleted. Earlier editions' contents were not checked; the licence was not stated on the page read.
